LESSON: LINEAR EQUATIONS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: ALGEBRA
Topic 2.2: Linear Equations
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Linear Equations, part of ALGEBRA in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we use linear equations in real life? 2. Why do we use linear equations in real life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Linear Equations together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: A learner develops speaking, listening and team work as they role-play in groups on

activities involving equations in one unknown.

● Self-efficacy: A learner develops self-awareness skills as they carry out weighing using beam balance and role play.

● Learning to learn: A learner reflects on their own experiences as they apply linear equations in real life.

Values:
● Social justice: A learner enhances cooperation as they work out linear equations generated from role-play activities.

● Responsibility: A learner enhances self-drive as they role play activities involving equations with one unknown.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social cohesion: A learner works in groups to role play in shopping activities.

● Life skills and values-self-esteem: A learner participates in role-play activities like weighing and shopping that will lead

to equations in one unknown.

Link to other subjects:

● Pre-technical studies: A learner uses digital devices with assistive technology in forming and solving equations.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● Digital devices with assistive technology such as magnifiers, screen readers and adapted keyboards, Print and Braille
